title: Accepting, Declining and Expiry of Hardship Assistance Programs Offers
content:
Terms offered under the Hardship Assistance Programs take effect only when the borrower accepts and e-signs them; a representative cannot accept on the borrower's behalf.

## Acceptance period

The borrower can accept the offered terms only when the current date is no later than the decision date plus the program's offer acceptance days. The acceptance period is counted in calendar days starting the day after the decision date, and acceptance on the last day is in time. The decision date is the one recorded on the plan.

| Decision date (hypothetical) | Offer acceptance days | Last day to accept | Acceptance on the last day | Acceptance the day after |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| 1 June | 10 | 11 June | in time | not available |
| 1 June | 14 | 15 June | in time | not available |

## What happens to an offer

| Event | Result |
|---|---|
| The borrower accepts and e-signs within the period | the plan becomes active |
| The period ends without acceptance | the offer expires |
| The borrower turns the offer down at any time before it expires | the offer closes as cancelled |

## AutoPay

Accepting a plan does not cancel AutoPay. For a plan with a plan installment, the AutoPay debit amount becomes the plan installment; for a deferral, no debit is taken on a deferred due date.

## Programs without acceptance

Whether a program needs the borrower's acceptance, and how many days its acceptance period runs, are given per program in the documents, decision and acceptance timetable; a Disaster Relief Deferral and a Servicemember Rate Cap Benefit are applied without an acceptance step.
